style: Refine every catalog object toward warm, softly lit cartoon art, consistent with the selected plant reference. Preserve identity, function and original palette family. Keep registered camera, dimensions, roots, sockets, ports, footprints and animation timing. No preferred horizontal light direction for rotatable world sprites; no directional ground shadows. Real 3D render output, editable Blender sources. The source 2D effects remain explicitly identified as 2D. Each object receives fresh independent editor/judge agents. Publish object-by-object to the same PR preview; integrate approved sprites into Godot after catalog review checks. Follow-on design exploration: improve the modeling itself, including forms, proportions, structure, crafted details and decorations. Original part counts and awkward geometry are not constraints. The editor may rebuild native geometry to achieve the better design; the judge should reward useful improvements. Preserve the locked registration, gameplay contact/clearance, animation and modular continuity contract. See modeling-policy.json version2.

Reject target drift only when it harms the chosen style, readability, role or locked technical contract. Original part counts and weak shapes are not automatically constraints.

outcomes: The green beret reads as a soft folded cap with a coherent crown, band and controlled top detail; broad volume replaces the source's abrupt wedge planes without spikes, self-intersecting layers or an inflated silhouette outside the functional envelope.

Blueblack fringe and side/back hair have coherent rounded volume and deliberate overlap. Front locks frame the face, profiles retain a clear ear/face opening, and rear hair has form rather than an undifferentiated black slab.

The mediumtan face and hands have soft, purposeful edges; eyes, cheeks, nose and smile remain friendly and distinguishable at logical display size. Changes to proportions can improve the design while respecting identity, envelope and rig contacts.

Ivory coat and plum apron read as constructed garments around the body. Collar, sleeve/cuff, apron edge/straps and useful pocket or tie detail have clear hierarchy; purposeful decoration is welcome when it strengthens the chef role and remains legible.
All four facings describe one consistent modeled character. Rear/profile surfaces show sufficient volume and construction; no unseen target feature is invented as a mandatory requirement.
Noor remains mediumtan/amber-skinned with blueblack fringe/sidehair, a green folded-band beret, ivory coat, plum apron and necktie, and dark shoes.

The large green, blueblack, skin, ivory and plum areas remain clearly separated and retain the original palette family. Warm shading may enrich them but may not turn the hat yellow/brown, the hair brown, the skin into a different identity, or the apron/tie into the family concept's blue/red.
Plum tie/pocket/straps and dark shoes retain enough value or form separation to read, while the coat keeps ivory midtones and does not become a blown white patch.
Broad warm illumination and soft transitions reveal the beret, hair, face and garment volumes; the figure is neither flat/emissive nor dominated by hard angular face bands.

Highlights are controlled and broad enough to suit the warm cartoon reference. Hair retains visible blueblack form and skin retains readable midtones; no deep black dead spots, blown coat/eye highlights or wet metallic cloth distract from the face.

One horizontally symmetric native light/material treatment works for every rotation. No preferred horizontal key direction, per-facing recoloring, directional ground shadow or painted glow is introduced.

Large clothing and headwear details look intentional, with clean edge transitions and restrained material variation; details support volume and chef identity at use size instead of becoming speckle or visual clutter.

Skin, hair and cloth have subtly distinct, compatible response to light. Micro-grain, target imagegen noise and exact target fastener counts are optional and cannot substitute for readable modeled forms.
The body remains an editable native model. The existing salmon cutout remains explicitly 2D with stable UV/alpha and native attachment, while the work utensil remains native geometry.

At logical 192x320 frames and the fixed 128-pixel cell calibration, the silhouette, face, cap, apron, arms/hands and shoes remain recognizable. Useful new volume/detail survives the native scale without enlarging or fitting the character in the frame.

Light, gray and dark composites show genuine transparency with clean edges: no target halo, colored fringe, opaque rectangle, floating shadow, black cracks, noisy boundaries, missing corners or alpha holes.
Every required facing/frame is free from visible clipping, self-intersection, coplanar shimmer, detached parts, abrupt normals/seams, disappearing detail, stretched garments and texture swimming.
Added or rebuilt geometry does not materially conceal the face, evaluated hand/knife contact, dish readability or planted foot contact beyond the original source attachment arrangement.

All four original 12-frame states remain visibly alive and coherent at 12fps in all four actual facings. Idle, work and hold close smoothly; load retains its non-loop flag and original out-and-back reach with dish visible throughout.

Feet stay planted as in the source, garments and hair track their rig without popping, hands retain their source actions, the knife appears only during work, and the dish appears only in hold/load with the authored attachment behavior.
No invented walking, stationary workstation geometry, one-way load trajectory or dish release is required or authorized by these criteria.
